model_answer: Add them when the reading is separate and long, so the parent's context stays clear. Against: each reader is a loop with its own bill, and a reader can fail, time out or repeat work. I would start with one parent, give each reader a brief that names its file and its field, and check each answer before I rely on it.
prompt: Your task needs five files read. Would you add sub-agents? Argue for and against, and say what you would check.
rubric: Gives an honest reason: separate, long work, or context isolation
Names the cost of a sub-agent: its own loop and input
Says what happens when a sub-agent fails or times out
Says how the parent checks the answers it gets back

model_answer: One agent is cheaper and easier to follow, but its one context fills with every step. An orchestrator with workers spreads reading across several contexts, and it adds cost and new failures: a brief that drops a constraint, and workers that repeat each other. Workers get an isolated context when they need only their brief; they get a forked one when the parent's messages decide their work.
prompt: Compare one agent with an orchestrator and workers on cost and failure. Which context do the workers get, and why?
rubric: Compares cost and the failure modes of the two shapes
Names a failure of the orchestrator shape: a dropped constraint or repeated work
Chooses isolated or forked for a stated reason
Says what the parent gets back, and how it checks it
